newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks surge on Dow, primary rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks surge on Dow, primary rate hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended sharply up on Tuesday in tandem with a rally on Wall Street and expected sharp falls in primary interest rates, with key blue chips leading the charge on favorable earnings forecasts, traders and analysts said.
"The bourse was livlier today, with the Dow (Jones) setting the pace, as it ususally does," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index .MXX ended up 56.99 points, or 1.52 percent, at 3,815.53.
The Dow Jones soared 173.38 points, it's second largest gain ever, to 6,833.59 points.
"Secondary (Money market) rates fell very sharply, which fuels hopes that primaries will be down this evening," a desk trader said.

Overnight rates on Cetes ended down 290 basis points at 18.50 percent, dealers said. Money market traders surveyed by Reuters forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 21.22 percent at the primary auction due later in the day. This would represent a fall of 139 basis points since last week's auction.
"Telmex led the way, followed by Cifra. Telmex earnings are due tomorrow, or the day after at the latest and they are expected to be favorable," Copca said.
"Cifra also gained, partly, on earnings expectations," he added.
Telecomms firm Telmex L shares gained 38 centavos to 16.58 pesos, while its ADRs ended up 7/8 at 41-7/8. Retail chain Cifra B shares rose 42 centavos to 12.10 pesos.
"Cifra had also been hit very hard and the retail sector in general looks like posting good earnings," a trader said.
Dealers nonetheless noted trading volume .TV.MX was restrained at 75.3 million shares, as the money market had drawn more capital flow.
Traders also drew attention to falls on shares listed by Mexico's two largest financial stocks, GFB B and Banacci.
"GFB and Banacci do not look like posting such good reports," a desk trader said.
GFB and Banacci bucked the overall trend on the bourse to close at session lows. GFB ended off five centavos at 2.67 pesos, while Banacci fell 18 centavos to 16.80 pesos.
Corn flour and tortilla firm Maseca gained 30 centavos to 7.74 pesos in brisk trade.

"Maseca gained on news of a possible cut in the tortilla subsidiary," one trader said, referring to a press report Maseca's director general expected the government to lift price controls on tortillas, a basic Mexican staple.
"Maseca gained on a technical rebound," another trader said.
On the broad market, of 108 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered decliners by 62 to 28.
